title: Rohit Sharma Thanks Bharat Army for 'Rock Solid' Support Ahead of Fourth ODI
excerpt: In a video message shared by the Bharat Army, Rohit signed a 'Thank You Bharat Army' jersey as India, leading New Zealand 2-0, prepare for the fourth ODI at Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui, on Friday.
body:
• Rohit Sharma thanked the Bharat Army in a video message shared on the fan group's Instagram, signing a Bharat Army jersey carrying the words 'Thank You Bharat Army'.
  • India lead the five-match ODI series against New Zealand 2-0, after winning the first two matches and seeing the third, in Hamilton, abandoned because of rain.
  • The fourth ODI is on Friday, November 13, at Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui; India need one more win to take the series.
  • Shreyas Iyer will captain India in the final two ODIs, with Ishan Kishan as his deputy, as Shubman Gill and KL Rahul leave to prepare for the Test series, per CricInformer.

Rohit Sharma has thanked the Bharat Army for standing behind the Indian team through victories and difficult moments alike, in a video message shared by the supporters' group ahead of the fourth ODI against New Zealand in Mount Maunganui. In the video, Rohit is seen signing a Bharat Army jersey marked 'Thank You Bharat Army', ANI reported.

"You've been rock solid in terms of getting behind us and supporting us. So we wouldn't expect anything less than what you've been doing over the years. So thank you again."

— Rohit Sharma, in a video message to the Bharat Army

Why the message, and why now

The Bharat Army is the organised global community of Indian cricket supporters that follows the team on overseas tours, and its members have been a visible presence through this series in New Zealand. Rohit's message acknowledged supporters who have followed the team across countries and stood behind the players in both directions of results, and urged them to keep doing so in the years ahead, MyKhel reported.

The series state

India won the opening two ODIs to lead the five-match series 2-0; the third match, at Seddon Park in Hamilton, was abandoned without play because of rain. The fourth ODI follows on Friday, November 13, at Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui, where a win would give India an unassailable 3-0 lead with one match to spare. New Zealand must win both remaining matches to level the series 2-2. India will field a changed side for the last two games: Shreyas Iyer takes over the captaincy from Shubman Gill, with Ishan Kishan as vice-captain, while Mitchell Santner continues to lead New Zealand.
nri_angle: The Bharat Army is the diaspora's travelling fan community; Rohit's message was aimed at supporters who follow India across overseas tours.
author: Diaspora Desk
